<script type="application/json" id="pack-y3w06">{"year":3,"week":6,"id":"y3w06","title":"Quadratic Equations I: Factorisation, the Formula and Real-Life Problems","subtitle":"Recognising quadratic equations; solving by factorisation (common factor, grouping, difference of two squares), by completing the square and by the quadratic formula; the discriminant and the nature of the roots; sum and product of roots; and forming and solving quadratic equations from real situations, rejecting answers that do not fit the context.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Algebraic Reasoning: Quadratics and Graphs","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":6,"to":9},"outcomes":["Decide whether a given equation is quadratic and write it in the standard form $ax^2+bx+c=0$.","Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, including the method of grouping.","Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and by the quadratic formula, and derive the formula.","Use the discriminant $b^2-4ac$ to describe the nature of the roots.","Use the sum and product of roots to evaluate expressions and form equations with given roots.","Form quadratic equations from real-life problems, solve them and interpret the solutions in context."],"keywords":["quadratic equation","standard form","coefficient","root","solution","zero-product property","factorisation","grouping","difference of two squares","perfect square","completing the square","quadratic formula","discriminant","real roots","repeated root","irrational roots","sum of roots","product of roots","modelling"],"notes":[{"title":"What is a quadratic equation?","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Quadratic equation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **quadratic equation** in $x$ is an equation that can be written as"},{"k":"math","tex":"ax^2+bx+c=0,\\qquad a\\neq0,"},{"k":"p","text":"where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants. It is a polynomial equation of **degree 2**: the highest power of the variable is 2."}]},{"k":"ul","items":["$a\\neq0$ is essential: if $a=0$ the equation is linear, $bx+c=0$.","To decide whether an equation is quadratic, first clear fractions and brackets and collect all terms on one side. For example $(1-x)^2=9$ becomes $x^2-2x-8=0$ (quadratic), but $x^2+x-4+\\dfrac1x=0$ becomes $x^3+x^2-4x+1=0$ (cubic)."]},{"k":"p","text":"The **roots** (solutions) are the values of $x$ that make the equation true. Graphically, they are the $x$-intercepts of $y=ax^2+bx+c$ (Week 7)."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-roots","caption":"The roots are where the graph crosses the $x$-axis."}],"figs":["w06-roots"]},{"title":"Solving by factorisation","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"The zero-product property","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If $PQ=0$, then $P=0$ or $Q=0$. So once $ax^2+bx+c$ is written as a product of two linear factors, each factor is set equal to zero."}]},{"k":"p","text":"Always **rearrange to make one side zero first**. From $x^2=5x$ we get $x^2-5x=0$, $x(x-5)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=5$. Dividing both sides by $x$ would lose the root $x=0$."},{"k":"p","text":"**The method of grouping** for $ax^2+bx+c=0$:"},{"k":"ol","items":["Find $ac$.","Find two numbers whose **product is $ac$** and whose **sum is $b$**.","Split $bx$ using these numbers.","Group the terms in pairs and take out the common factor of each pair.","Take out the common bracket, then set each factor equal to zero."]},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-areamodel","caption":"An area model of $2x^2+7x+3=(2x+1)(x+3)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Special factorisations","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["common factor: $ax^2+bx=x(ax+b)$","difference of two squares: $p^2x^2-q^2=(px-q)(px+q)$","perfect squares: $x^2\\pm2kx+k^2=(x\\pm k)^2$"]}]}],"figs":["w06-areamodel"]},{"title":"Completing the square","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$x^2+bx$ is completed to a perfect square by adding $\\left(\\dfrac b2\\right)^2$:"},{"k":"math","tex":"x^2+bx=\\left(x+\\frac b2\\right)^2-\\left(\\frac b2\\right)^2."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-square","caption":"Half of 6 is 3, and the missing corner is $3^2=9$."},{"k":"p","text":"To solve $ax^2+bx+c=0$ by completing the square: divide by $a$, move the constant to the right, add $\\left(\\tfrac{b}{2a}\\right)^2$ to both sides, then take square roots (remembering $\\pm$)."}],"figs":["w06-square"]},{"title":"The quadratic formula","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Completing the square on $ax^2+bx+c=0$ gives the general solution."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"The quadratic formula","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"x=\\frac{-b\\pm\\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}"}]},{"k":"p","text":"The formula works for **every** quadratic equation, including those that do not factorise. Write the equation in standard form first, and take care with signs: for $2x^2-x-1=0$, $b=-1$ and $-b=1$."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"The discriminant","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The expression $D=b^2-4ac$ under the square root is the **discriminant**. It tells us the nature of the roots without solving."},{"k":"table","head":["$D=b^2-4ac$","Roots","Graph of $y=ax^2+bx+c$"],"rows":[["$D>0$","two distinct real roots","crosses the $x$-axis twice"],["$D=0$","one repeated real root $x=-\\dfrac{b}{2a}$","touches the $x$-axis"],["$D<0$","no real roots","does not meet the $x$-axis"]]},{"k":"p","text":"If $D>0$ is a perfect square (and $a$, $b$, $c$ are integers), the roots are **rational** and the quadratic factorises."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-discriminant","caption":"The sign of the discriminant decides the number of real roots."}],"figs":["w06-discriminant"]},{"title":"Sum and product of roots","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ are the roots of $ax^2+bx+c=0$, then $ax^2+bx+c=a(x-\\alpha)(x-\\beta)$, and comparing coefficients:"},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Sum and product","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"\\alpha+\\beta=-\\frac ba,\\qquad\\alpha\\beta=\\frac ca."},{"k":"p","text":"An equation with roots $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ is $x^2-(\\alpha+\\beta)x+\\alpha\\beta=0$."},{"k":"p","text":"Useful identities: $\\alpha^2+\\beta^2=(\\alpha+\\beta)^2-2\\alpha\\beta$ and $\\dfrac1\\alpha+\\dfrac1\\beta=\\dfrac{\\alpha+\\beta}{\\alpha\\beta}$."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Real-life problems","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Modelling with quadratics","blocks":[{"k":"ol","items":["Choose a letter for the unknown and state its units.","Write the facts as an equation (area, Pythagoras, time = distance ÷ speed, cost ÷ number).","Rearrange into standard form and solve.","**Check each root against the context**: lengths, numbers of people and speeds must be positive, and other quantities in the problem must stay sensible.","Answer the question in words, with units."]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Where quadratic equations arise","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Areas of plots, rooms and frames; the paths of thrown balls and water jets; Pythagoras in ladders, roofs and masts; speed–time problems; and sharing costs or goods among a changing number of people all lead to quadratic equations."}]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Is it quadratic?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Which of these are quadratic equations? For each one, give $a$, $b$ and $c$. (a) $x^2+3x=0$ (b) $3x^2-5x+7=0$ (c) $x^3-x=2$ (d) $x+1-\\dfrac4x=0$ (e) $(1-x)^2=9$ (f) $2x+\\dfrac3x=1$ (g) $8x^2=0$"}],"steps":["(a) Yes: $a=1$, $b=3$, $c=0$.","(b) Yes: $a=3$, $b=-5$, $c=7$.","(c) No: the highest power is 3 (cubic).","(d) Multiply by $x$: $x^2+x-4=0$. Yes: $a=1$, $b=1$, $c=-4$ (with $x\\neq0$).","(e) $1-2x+x^2=9$, so $x^2-2x-8=0$. Yes: $a=1$, $b=-2$, $c=-8$.","(f) Multiply by $x$: $2x^2+3=x$, so $2x^2-x+3=0$. Yes: $a=2$, $b=-1$, $c=3$.","(g) Yes: $a=8$, $b=0$, $c=0$."],"answer":"All except (c) are quadratic.","figs":[]},{"title":"Factorising by grouping","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $2x^2+3x-5=0$."}],"steps":["$a=2$, $b=3$, $c=-5$, so $ac=-10$.","Two numbers with product $-10$ and sum $3$: $5$ and $-2$.","Split the middle term: $2x^2+5x-2x-5=0$.","Group: $x(2x+5)-1(2x+5)=0$.","Factorise: $(2x+5)(x-1)=0$.","$2x+5=0$ gives $x=-\\dfrac52$; $x-1=0$ gives $x=1$.","Check $x=1$: $2+3-5=0$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=-2\\tfrac12$ or $x=1$","figs":[]},{"title":"A harder grouping","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $6x^2-11x-10=0$."}],"steps":["$ac=6\\times(-10)=-60$. Numbers with product $-60$ and sum $-11$: $-15$ and $4$.","$6x^2-15x+4x-10=0$.","$3x(2x-5)+2(2x-5)=0$.","$(3x+2)(2x-5)=0$.","$x=-\\dfrac23$ or $x=\\dfrac52$."],"answer":"$x=-\\tfrac23$ or $x=2\\tfrac12$","figs":[]},{"title":"Special cases","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve (a) $4x^2-9=0$ (b) $3x^2+8x=0$ (c) $9x^2-30x+25=0$."}],"steps":["(a) Difference of two squares: $(2x)^2-3^2=(2x-3)(2x+3)=0$, so $x=\\pm\\dfrac32$.","(b) Common factor: $x(3x+8)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=-\\dfrac83$.","(c) Perfect square: $9x^2-30x+25=(3x-5)^2=0$, so $x=\\dfrac53$ (a repeated root)."],"answer":"(a) $\\pm1\\tfrac12$ (b) $0$ or $-2\\tfrac23$ (c) $1\\tfrac23$ (repeated)","figs":[]},{"title":"Completing the square","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve by completing the square: (a) $x^2+6x-7=0$ (b) $2x^2-8x+3=0$, giving answers to 2 decimal places."}],"steps":["(a) $x^2+6x=7$. Add $\\left(\\tfrac62\\right)^2=9$: $x^2+6x+9=16$, so $(x+3)^2=16$.","$x+3=\\pm4$, so $x=1$ or $x=-7$.","(b) Divide by 2: $x^2-4x+\\dfrac32=0$, so $x^2-4x=-\\dfrac32$.","Add $\\left(\\tfrac{-4}{2}\\right)^2=4$: $(x-2)^2=\\dfrac52$.","$x-2=\\pm\\sqrt{\\tfrac52}=\\pm1.581$, so $x=3.58$ or $x=0.42$."],"answer":"(a) $1$ or $-7$ (b) $3.58$ or $0.42$","figs":[]},{"title":"Using the formula","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve (a) $2x^2-x-1=0$ (b) $x^2+4x-21=0$ (c) $3x^2-5x-1=0$, correct to 2 decimal places."}],"steps":["(a) $a=2$, $b=-1$, $c=-1$: $x=\\dfrac{1\\pm\\sqrt{1+8}}{4}=\\dfrac{1\\pm3}{4}$, so $x=1$ or $x=-\\dfrac12$.","(b) $a=1$, $b=4$, $c=-21$: $x=\\dfrac{-4\\pm\\sqrt{16+84}}{2}=\\dfrac{-4\\pm10}{2}$, so $x=3$ or $x=-7$.","(c) $a=3$, $b=-5$, $c=-1$: $x=\\dfrac{5\\pm\\sqrt{25+12}}{6}=\\dfrac{5\\pm\\sqrt{37}}{6}$.","$\\sqrt{37}\\approx6.083$, so $x\\approx\\dfrac{11.083}{6}=1.85$ or $x\\approx\\dfrac{-1.083}{6}=-0.18$."],"answer":"(a) $1$, $-\\tfrac12$ (b) $3$, $-7$ (c) $1.85$, $-0.18$","figs":[]},{"title":"The nature of the roots","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Without solving, describe the roots of: (i) $x^2-6x+9=0$ (ii) $2x^2+3x+4=0$ (iii) $3x^2-2x-5=0$. (b) Find $k$ if $kx^2-12x+9=0$ has equal roots, and find the root."}],"steps":["(a)(i) $D=36-36=0$: one repeated root ($x=3$).","(ii) $D=9-32=-23<0$: no real roots.","(iii) $D=4+60=64>0$ and a perfect square: two distinct rational roots ($x=\\tfrac53$ and $x=-1$).","(b) Equal roots need $D=0$: $144-36k=0$, $k=4$.","Then $4x^2-12x+9=(2x-3)^2=0$, so $x=\\dfrac32$."],"answer":"(a) repeated; none; two rational (b) $k=4$, root $1\\tfrac12$","figs":[]},{"title":"Sum and product of roots","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ are the roots of $2x^2-7x+4=0$. Without solving, find (a) $\\alpha+\\beta$ and $\\alpha\\beta$ (b) $\\alpha^2+\\beta^2$ (c) $\\dfrac1\\alpha+\\dfrac1\\beta$ (d) $(\\alpha-\\beta)^2$."}],"steps":["(a) $\\alpha+\\beta=-\\dfrac{-7}{2}=\\dfrac72$; $\\alpha\\beta=\\dfrac42=2$.","(b) $\\alpha^2+\\beta^2=(\\alpha+\\beta)^2-2\\alpha\\beta=\\dfrac{49}{4}-4=\\dfrac{33}{4}$.","(c) $\\dfrac{\\alpha+\\beta}{\\alpha\\beta}=\\dfrac{7/2}{2}=\\dfrac74$.","(d) $(\\alpha-\\beta)^2=(\\alpha+\\beta)^2-4\\alpha\\beta=\\dfrac{49}{4}-8=\\dfrac{17}{4}$."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac72$, $2$ (b) $\\tfrac{33}{4}$ (c) $\\tfrac74$ (d) $\\tfrac{17}{4}$","figs":[]},{"title":"Forming an equation from its roots","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Form quadratic equations with integer coefficients whose roots are (a) $-\\dfrac23$ and $5$ (b) $2+\\sqrt3$ and $2-\\sqrt3$."}],"steps":["(a) Sum $=-\\dfrac23+5=\\dfrac{13}{3}$; product $=-\\dfrac{10}{3}$.","$x^2-\\dfrac{13}{3}x-\\dfrac{10}{3}=0$; multiply by 3: $3x^2-13x-10=0$.","Check: $(3x+2)(x-5)=3x^2-13x-10$ ✓.","(b) Sum $=4$; product $=(2+\\sqrt3)(2-\\sqrt3)=4-3=1$.","$x^2-4x+1=0$."],"answer":"(a) $3x^2-13x-10=0$ (b) $x^2-4x+1=0$","figs":[]},{"title":"A rectangular plate","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A rectangular metal plate has an area of 6 m² and a perimeter of 11 m. Find its dimensions."}],"steps":["Let the length be $L$ m and the width $W$ m: $LW=6$ and $2L+2W=11$.","From the first, $W=\\dfrac6L$. Substitute: $2L+\\dfrac{12}{L}=11$.","Multiply by $L$: $2L^2+12=11L$, so $2L^2-11L+12=0$.","$ac=24$; numbers $-3$ and $-8$: $2L^2-3L-8L+12=L(2L-3)-4(2L-3)=(2L-3)(L-4)=0$.","$L=4$ or $L=\\dfrac32$. If $L=4$, $W=\\dfrac64=\\dfrac32$; if $L=\\dfrac32$, $W=4$: the same rectangle.","Check: area $4\\times1.5=6$ ✓; perimeter $2(4+1.5)=11$ ✓."],"answer":"4 m by 1.5 m","figs":[]},{"title":"A 40 km walk","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Esi took part in a 40 km walk. She walked the first 16 km at $x$ km/h and the rest at $(x-2)$ km/h. Her total time was 6 hours. Find $x$ and the time for each stage."}],"steps":["Time $=\\dfrac{\\text{distance}}{\\text{speed}}$: first stage $\\dfrac{16}{x}$ h; second stage $\\dfrac{24}{x-2}$ h.","$\\dfrac{16}{x}+\\dfrac{24}{x-2}=6$. Multiply by $x(x-2)$: $16(x-2)+24x=6x(x-2)$.","$40x-32=6x^2-12x$, so $6x^2-52x+32=0$, and dividing by 2, $3x^2-26x+16=0$.","$(3x-2)(x-8)=0$, so $x=8$ or $x=\\dfrac23$.","If $x=\\dfrac23$, the second speed $x-2$ is negative: reject. So $x=8$ km/h.","Times: $\\dfrac{16}{8}=2$ h and $\\dfrac{24}{6}=4$ h; total 6 h ✓."],"answer":"$x=8$ km/h; 2 h and 4 h","figs":["w06-walk"]},{"title":"A path round a garden","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A rectangular garden 20 m by 12 m is surrounded by a path of uniform width $x$ m. The total area of the garden and the path is 384 m². Find the width of the path and the area of the path."}],"steps":["The outer rectangle is $(20+2x)$ m by $(12+2x)$ m.","$(20+2x)(12+2x)=384$, so $240+64x+4x^2=384$.","$4x^2+64x-144=0$; divide by 4: $x^2+16x-36=0$.","$(x+18)(x-2)=0$, so $x=2$ (the width cannot be $-18$).","Area of path $=384-20\\times12=384-240=144$ m²."],"answer":"Width 2 m; path area 144 m²","figs":["w06-garden"]},{"title":"A ladder against a wall","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A 13 m ladder leans against a vertical wall. The top of the ladder is 7 m higher above the ground than the foot is from the wall. How far is the foot from the wall?"}],"steps":["Let the foot be $x$ m from the wall; the top is $(x+7)$ m up.","Pythagoras: $x^2+(x+7)^2=13^2$, so $2x^2+14x+49=169$.","$2x^2+14x-120=0$, and $x^2+7x-60=0$.","$(x+12)(x-5)=0$, so $x=5$ (reject $-12$).","The foot is 5 m from the wall and the top is 12 m up. Check: $5^2+12^2=169$ ✓."],"answer":"5 m","figs":["w06-ladder"]},{"title":"Consecutive odd numbers","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 575. Find the numbers."}],"steps":["Let the numbers be $n$ and $n+2$: $n(n+2)=575$, so $n^2+2n-575=0$.","$D=4+2300=2304=48^2$, so $n=\\dfrac{-2\\pm48}{2}=23$ or $-25$.","The numbers are 23 and 25, or $-25$ and $-23$.","Check: $23\\times25=575$ ✓ and $(-25)(-23)=575$ ✓."],"answer":"23 and 25 (or $-25$ and $-23$)","figs":[]},{"title":"Sharing the cost of sugar","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A trader spent GH₵1200 on bags of sugar. If each bag had cost GH₵20 less, she could have bought 5 more bags for the same money. How many bags did she buy, and at what price?"}],"steps":["Let her buy $n$ bags: price per bag $=\\dfrac{1200}{n}$.","At GH₵20 less she buys $n+5$ bags: $\\dfrac{1200}{n}-\\dfrac{1200}{n+5}=20$.","Multiply by $n(n+5)$: $1200(n+5)-1200n=20n(n+5)$, so $6000=20n^2+100n$.","$n^2+5n-300=0$, $(n+20)(n-15)=0$, so $n=15$.","Price $=\\dfrac{1200}{15}=80$, that is GH₵80 a bag. Check: $\\dfrac{1200}{20}=60=80-20$ ✓."],"answer":"15 bags at GH₵80 each","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Key results","items":["Standard form $ax^2+bx+c=0$, $a\\neq0$; make one side zero before factorising.","Grouping: find two numbers with product $ac$ and sum $b$.","Completing the square: $x^2+bx=\\left(x+\\tfrac b2\\right)^2-\\left(\\tfrac b2\\right)^2$.","Formula: $x=\\dfrac{-b\\pm\\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$.","Discriminant $D=b^2-4ac$: $D>0$ two roots, $D=0$ one repeated root, $D<0$ no real roots.","$\\alpha+\\beta=-\\tfrac ba$, $\\alpha\\beta=\\tfrac ca$; equation $x^2-(\\alpha+\\beta)x+\\alpha\\beta=0$.","In applications, reject roots that do not fit the context."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"Which of these is a quadratic equation?","options":["$(x+2)^2=7$","$x^3+x=1$","$3x+2=0$","$\\dfrac1x=4$"],"correct":0,"explain":"It expands to $x^2+4x-3=0$."},{"q":"The roots of $(x-4)(2x+3)=0$ are","options":["$4$ and $-\\tfrac32$","$-4$ and $\\tfrac32$","$4$ and $-3$","$-4$ and $-\\tfrac32$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Set each factor equal to zero."},{"q":"To factorise $3x^2+10x-8$ by grouping, the two numbers needed are","options":["$12$ and $-2$","$8$ and $-1$","$4$ and $-6$","$-12$ and $2$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Product $ac=-24$ and sum $10$."},{"q":"To complete the square for $x^2-10x$, add","options":["25","100","10","5"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\left(\\tfrac{-10}{2}\\right)^2=25$."},{"q":"The discriminant of $2x^2-5x+3=0$ is","options":["1","49","$-1$","13"],"correct":0,"explain":"$25-24=1$."},{"q":"The equation $x^2+4x+k=0$ has equal roots when $k=$","options":["4","2","16","$-4$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$16-4k=0$."},{"q":"If $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ are the roots of $3x^2-6x-2=0$, then $\\alpha\\beta=$","options":["$-\\tfrac23$","$2$","$-2$","$\\tfrac23$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\alpha\\beta=\\tfrac ca$."},{"q":"A quadratic with roots $3$ and $-5$ is","options":["$x^2+2x-15=0$","$x^2-2x-15=0$","$x^2+2x+15=0$","$x^2-8x+15=0$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Sum $-2$, product $-15$."},{"q":"Solving $x^2=6x$ by dividing both sides by $x$ is wrong because","options":["it loses the root $x=0$","it gives a negative root","$x^2$ cannot be divided","the equation is not quadratic"],"correct":0,"explain":"Correct: $x(x-6)=0$, so $x=0$ or $6$."},{"q":"A rectangle has length $(x+3)$ m, width $x$ m and area 40 m². Then $x=$","options":["5","8","4","10"],"correct":0,"explain":"$x^2+3x-40=(x+8)(x-5)=0$."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Solve $x^2-x-42=0$.","a":"$x=7$ or $x=-6$"},{"q":"Solve $5x^2+13x-6=0$.","a":"$(5x-2)(x+3)=0$: $x=\\tfrac25$ or $-3$"},{"q":"Solve $25x^2-16=0$ and $7x^2=21x$.","a":"$\\pm\\tfrac45$; $0$ or $3$"},{"q":"Solve $x^2-8x+5=0$ by completing the square, to 2 d.p.","a":"$(x-4)^2=11$: $7.32$, $0.68$"},{"q":"Solve $2x^2+5x-4=0$ by the formula, to 2 d.p.","a":"$\\dfrac{-5\\pm\\sqrt{57}}{4}$: $0.64$, $-3.14$"},{"q":"For what values of $p$ does $x^2+px+16=0$ have equal roots?","a":"$p=\\pm8$"},{"q":"Show that $x^2-2x+5=0$ has no real roots.","a":"$D=4-20=-16<0$"},{"q":"If $\\alpha$, $\\beta$ are the roots of $x^2-5x+3=0$, find $\\alpha^2+\\beta^2$ and $\\dfrac{\\beta}{\\alpha}+\\dfrac{\\alpha}{\\beta}$.","a":"$19$; $\\tfrac{19}{3}$"},{"q":"Form an equation with roots $\\tfrac12$ and $-\\tfrac34$.","a":"$8x^2+2x-3=0$"},{"q":"The sum of a number and its reciprocal is $\\tfrac{10}{3}$. Find the number.","a":"$3$ or $\\tfrac13$"},{"q":"A right-angled triangle has sides $x$, $(x+7)$ and $(x+8)$ cm. Find $x$.","a":"$x^2-2x-15=0$: $x=5$ (sides 5, 12, 13)"},{"q":"Solve $x^4-13x^2+36=0$ (let $u=x^2$).","a":"$u=4$ or $9$: $x=\\pm2$, $\\pm3$"}],"theory":[{"q":"(a) By completing the square on $ax^2+bx+c=0$, derive the quadratic formula. (b) Use it to explain why $D=b^2-4ac<0$ gives no real roots. (c) Show that the two roots always add up to $-\\dfrac ba$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Divide by $a$: $x^2+\\dfrac bax+\\dfrac ca=0$, so $x^2+\\dfrac bax=-\\dfrac ca$."},{"k":"p","text":"Add $\\left(\\dfrac{b}{2a}\\right)^2$ to both sides: $\\left(x+\\dfrac{b}{2a}\\right)^2=\\dfrac{b^2}{4a^2}-\\dfrac ca=\\dfrac{b^2-4ac}{4a^2}$."},{"k":"p","text":"Take square roots: $x+\\dfrac{b}{2a}=\\pm\\dfrac{\\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$, so $x=\\dfrac{-b\\pm\\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) The left side $\\left(x+\\tfrac{b}{2a}\\right)^2$ is a square, so it cannot be negative for real $x$. If $b^2-4ac<0$, the right side is negative, so no real $x$ works."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) $\\dfrac{-b+\\sqrt D}{2a}+\\dfrac{-b-\\sqrt D}{2a}=\\dfrac{-2b}{2a}=-\\dfrac ba$."}]},{"q":"A rectangular sheet of metal measures 30 cm by 20 cm. Equal squares of side $x$ cm are cut from each corner and the sides are folded up to make an open box. The area of the base of the box is 336 cm². (a) Show that $x^2-25x+66=0$. (b) Solve the equation and explain which root is valid. (c) Find the volume of the box.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) The base measures $(30-2x)$ by $(20-2x)$ cm, so $(30-2x)(20-2x)=336$."},{"k":"p","text":"$600-100x+4x^2=336$, $4x^2-100x+264=0$; divide by 4: $x^2-25x+66=0$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $(x-3)(x-22)=0$, so $x=3$ or $x=22$. If $x=22$, the width $20-44$ is negative, which is impossible. So $x=3$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) The box is 24 cm by 14 cm by 3 cm: volume $=336\\times3=1008$ cm³."}]},{"q":"A group of students hired a bus for GH₵1800, to share the cost equally. Five students withdrew, so each of the others paid GH₵12 more. (a) Taking $n$ as the original number of students, form an equation and show that it simplifies to $n^2-5n-750=0$. (b) Find the original number of students and the amount each finally paid.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Original share $\\dfrac{1800}{n}$; new share $\\dfrac{1800}{n-5}$."},{"k":"p","text":"$\\dfrac{1800}{n-5}-\\dfrac{1800}{n}=12$. Multiply by $n(n-5)$: $1800n-1800(n-5)=12n(n-5)$."},{"k":"p","text":"$9000=12n^2-60n$; divide by 12: $750=n^2-5n$, so $n^2-5n-750=0$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $(n-30)(n+25)=0$, so $n=30$ (reject $-25$)."},{"k":"p","text":"Each of the 25 remaining students paid $\\dfrac{1800}{25}=72$, that is GH₵72 (GH₵12 more than GH₵60)."}]},{"q":"(a) Find the values of $k$ for which $x^2+(k-3)x+k=0$ has equal roots. (b) For each value, find the root. (c) For what values of $k$ does the equation have two distinct real roots?","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) $D=(k-3)^2-4k=k^2-10k+9=0$, so $(k-1)(k-9)=0$: $k=1$ or $k=9$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $k=1$: $x^2-2x+1=(x-1)^2=0$, root $x=1$. $k=9$: $x^2+6x+9=(x+3)^2=0$, root $x=-3$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Two distinct roots need $D>0$: $(k-1)(k-9)>0$, which holds when $k<1$ or $k>9$."}]},{"q":"$\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ are the roots of $x^2-5x+3=0$. (a) Find $\\alpha+\\beta$ and $\\alpha\\beta$. (b) Form the equation whose roots are $\\alpha^2$ and $\\beta^2$. (c) Form the equation whose roots are $\\alpha+\\dfrac1\\beta$ and $\\beta+\\dfrac1\\alpha$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) $\\alpha+\\beta=5$, $\\alpha\\beta=3$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) Sum $\\alpha^2+\\beta^2=25-6=19$; product $\\alpha^2\\beta^2=9$. Equation: $x^2-19x+9=0$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Sum $=(\\alpha+\\beta)+\\dfrac{\\alpha+\\beta}{\\alpha\\beta}=5+\\dfrac53=\\dfrac{20}{3}$."},{"k":"p","text":"Product $=\\left(\\alpha+\\dfrac1\\beta\\right)\\left(\\beta+\\dfrac1\\alpha\\right)=\\alpha\\beta+1+1+\\dfrac{1}{\\alpha\\beta}=3+2+\\dfrac13=\\dfrac{16}{3}$."},{"k":"p","text":"Equation:
